items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The band leader was Jacques Largeaud and he had an amateur drummer who was a native from one of the oldest African tribes in Morocco, whose name was Slim. ... Slim couldn't believe his eyes, seeing Max Roach playing his old set of drums

ctx.x: The 21st of June, I did a concert in Joinville, a suburb of Paris with Benny Carter, Ben Webster, Kenny Drew, Art Taylor, Michel Sarbadi, Johnny Griffin, The Golden Gate Quartet. I could only make one concert because I had to leave the next day for Morocco, but there were going to be three concerts in the same theatre, the 21st, 22nd, and 23rd. On the programme would also be Claude Bolling, Memphis Slim, Slide Hampton, The Delta Rhytmn Boys. The festival was organized and sponsored by a woman named Lallie…

In Morocco, I went in Tanger to give a concert. The band leader was Jacques Largeaud and he had an amateur drummer who was a native from one of the oldest African tribes in Morocco, whose name was Slim. Slim had a very shabby set of drums.

During the intermission I was surprised to see Max Roach come into my dressing room. He was having a vacation in Tanger with his wife. It was nice to see him and during the second part of the show, I introduced him to the public and asked him to join me for a few numbers, and he accepted. It was a thrill. Slim couldn't believe his eyes, seeing Max Roach playing his old set of drums as if they were a new set just arrived from the factory.
